newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bangchak awards one MidEast crude, but not Oman.
newsitem.headline: Bangchak awards one MidEast crude, but not Oman.

text.p: Bangchak Petroleum Plc awarded just one Middle East crude cargo in its May buying tender, rejecting all offers of Oman crude, refinery sources said on Monday.

The 120,000 barrels-per-day Thai refinery did not award any Asian or West African crudes offered into the tender, but was carrying out separate negotiations with some of the companies that offered those crudes, the sources said.
They declined to name the crude which was awarded, but said it had similar characteristics to Dubai crude oil.
The refinery received four offers of Oman crude and the most competitive offer was MPM -3 cents, the sources said.

There were four offers of Qatar Marine, and one each of Iranian, Dubai and Arab Light. In earlier tenders this year, the refinery has awarded Iranian heavy crude oil in place of its usual Oman purchases.
Bangchak also received four offers of Tapis crude and one each of Thevenard, Barrow Island and Cossack.
It also received offers for Forcados, Palanca and Bonny light and medium crudes.
